From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Monthly monitoring signals & ops playbook

Team — attaching this month’s monitoring snapshot and the incident timeline. High-level notes up front: 

- Latency: P95 increased from 210ms -> 360ms on 9/10 during the midday traffic surge. Spike correlates with a config rollout (cache policy change) at 11:42 UTC.
- Cost: Token cost rose ~12% month-over-month; early signal points to increased long-tail sequences from two enterprise customers (ProdCo & CloudVendor).
- Uptime: Two transient 5–12 min pod restarts (9/8 & 9/11) attributed to driver oom under high concurrent KV loads.
- Usage: Daily active request growth +8% YOY; peak concurrency increased ~18%.

Action requests: please propose owners and remediation options in the thread by EOD. I suggest the following starting owners — Markus for latency, Neha for cost/cust billing tuning, Priyom for uptime/infra mitigations and QBR slide consolidation.

Attachments: [Attachment: sept_kpi_snapshot.xlsx (xlsx, 112KB)], [Attachment: incident_timeline.pdf (pdf, 85KB)]

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Platform Metrics | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Monthly monitoring signals & ops playbook

Thanks Laura — clear summary. I’ll take point on coordinating the QBR narrative and owners. Short notes / owners: 

- Latency (Markus): dig into rollout/config interaction and confirm whether prefix/KV cache invalidation occurred. If so, revert the policy for the next 24–48h and run a controlled canary.
- Cost (Neha): analyze long-tail requests by account (ProdCo, CloudVendor), estimate token delta and propose throttling/quotas or suggested prompt templates for customers.
- Uptime (Priyom): infra mitigation plan — bump driver memory ceil for high-concurrency pools and add pod-level healthcheck tuning.

For QBR: I need the latest slide deck. Laura, can you drop a copy of the QBR slide deck in the Drive link and flag which charts you want highlighted? I’ll produce a 2-slide executive summary for leadership. Target: draft by 9/15 EOD.

I’ll also loop in EngInfra if we need scheduled maintenance windows.

Attachments referenced: please add the deck as qbr_slide_deck_v3.pptx into the shared folder.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Production Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-14T14:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Monthly monitoring signals & ops playbook

Priyom / Laura — quick root-cause update on the latency P95: 

- Findings: During the 11:42 UTC rollout a new cache policy (eviction aggressiveness increased) was enabled in canary. That triggered a burst of KV cache misses for long-context requests causing extra backend calls and higher tail latency. Also saw a correlation with increased concurrent requests from ProdCo’s batch-run window.
- Immediate mitigation: rolling rollback of the cache policy in canary regions completed at 12:05 UTC; global rollback scheduled for 9/14 18:00 UTC if metrics don’t stabilize.
- Next steps (owners & ETA):
  - Revert global policy and monitor (Markus) — ETA 2 hours from approval.
  - Canary with warmed KV cache for 48 hours (Markus + Infra) — start after rollback.
  - Add a quick telemetry flag to highlight cache-miss rate by account (Neha will get account mapping to telemetry IDs).

I’ve attached a short note with charts and log snippets. If rollback isn’t possible without risking other regressions, propose a graduated reduction in eviction aggressiveness instead.

Attachments: [Attachment: latency_root_cause_notes.md (txt, 14KB)]

Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

- Neha: account-level cost delta and suggested mitigations (throttles, quota templates, or prompt guidance) — target 9/16 noon PT.
- Priyom: infra mitigations (driver memory ceil bump + healthcheck tuning) and final QBR 2-slide exec summary — draft by 9/15 EOD.
